timeout_lower_bound_336e8ae: SOUND. The deadline is stamped when the request is written inside the pump, which is before the test's t0, so the elapsed time measured from t0 can legitimately be a few ms short of the limit (599 vs 600). dt >= limit - 50 still rejects an early cancel (the mutant using the text timeout for voice gives a 300 ms cut against 600, i.e. 300 ms short, and is killed). Upper bound limit + 300 is unchanged.
flakiness_verdict: The busy-machine frame rule is a flaky test under extreme load, not a blocking bug. Evidence: (1) the reported failure had worst 8.8 ms and none at or over 50 ms; a real block in this bridge costs a whole timeout (300 ms or more) or a fixed 10-30 ms in every Nth poll, and the structural scan shows no blocking call is reachable from poll; (2) at 0.4/core the same hang cases show 0-2 polls over 5 ms, so the margin max(2, n/200) is thin; (3) a poll makes several syscalls (pipe reads, process probe) and the control makes one stat, so preemption hits the poll more often; (4) Ubuntu CI is green. Proposed fix (not shipped): make the control equal the poll in syscall mix, and/or skip the timing rule above about 2 load/core, leaving only the structural guard (but then the busy-loop mutants 'frame never blocked' would survive at that load, so prefer a wider relative allowance such as ctrl_slow + max(4, n/100), which still catches 4% of 10 ms polls). I tried a control with an open/read/process-probe/stat mix; my runs of it failed wholesale at load 49-53 (the service never handshook within the test's window), which I could not attribute, so I reverted it and changed no code. A change needs a quiet machine to validate against the 17 mutants.
non_blocking: Timing rule is load-sensitive: expect an occasional red on a very loaded local machine; rerun on a quiet one before treating it as a regression.
